answer: One defense is anchored commitments with delayed reveal: each agent must publish a hash of its identity to a shared atlas of registrants one full epoch before it may transact, and only then reveal the preimage. Because the registry is time-ordered, an attacker cannot spin up a hollow swarm the moment a reward appears; every fake identity costs a committed deposit, a waiting period, and a public slot that peers can audit. A single pearl of real work beats a thousand late registrations.
